summary: The root LQM primarily means to gobble or swallow a morsel quickly. It can also refer to putting morsels into one's mouth with the hand. The core idea is swift, often eager, consumption of food.
lane: 1 لَقِمَ لُقْمَةً ذ , [aor. لَقَمَ ,] inf. n. لَقْمٌ , (JK, MS,) [ He gobbled a gobbet, or morsel, or mouthful, or] he swallowed the gobbet; and so . (S.) لَقِمَهُ , aor. لَقَمَ , (Msb, K, &c.,) inf. n. لَقْمٌ , (JK, MA, K, MS, JM,) or لَقَمٌ (Msb, [app. a mistake,]) He gobbled it; i. e., ate it quickly, (Msb, K, TA,) as also , (Msb, [see above,]) and hastily; drew it with his mouth, and ate it quickly. (TA) -b2- لَقِمَ بِيَدِهِ He put morsels into his mouth (i. e., his own mouth) with his hand. See an ex. voce رَقَعَ . This seems to be the primary signification.

headwords.gloss: A morsel, gobbet; mouthful: what is; swallowed

parts.t: signifies what is swallowed at once in drinking: (Msb:) or

headwords.def: لُقْمَةٌ A morsel, gobbet, or mouthful: what is [ swallowed, or] eaten quickly, at once, of bread [&c.]; like as جُرْعَةٌ signifies what is swallowed at once in drinking: (Msb:) or what is prepared to be [ swallowed, or] eaten quickly [ at once ]. (K, TA.) لُقْمَةٌ القَاضِى , and لُقْمَةُ الخَلِيفَةِ : see زُمَاوَرْدٌ , art. ورد ; and مُيَسَّرٌ .
لُقَيْمَاتُ القَاضِى Same as لُقَمَاتُ القاضى .
